segments.description: Please welcome Professor Emeritus Natalia Stambulova, a globally recognized sport and exercise psychologist with over five decades of experience. Natalia's groundbreaking research on athletic career transitions has reshaped global practices in athlete development, emphasizing the balance of mental health and performance. Recipient of the 2021 Distinguished International Sports Psychologist Award, Natalia will share her expertise in her session, Navigating Transitions, a holistic approach to athlete development. Welcome, Natalia. Hello, everybody, and welcome here today. You're in for an absolute treat. We are going to talk to Dr. Natalia Stambulova. She's been an absolute trailblazer in athlete career talent development. She's published a whopping 200 publications, and there's been some groundbreaking research in there. And contextually today, we're going to talk about how this relates to tennis coaching in particular and how we look after our athletes. Welcome, Natalia. Hello, Paul. Hello, everybody. And thank you for inviting me to give this interview. As you mentioned, yes, I am an athlete career researcher for more than three decades. And that also influence the topic I suggest for today's interview, and the topic is career excellence in tennis. I am going to talk not about the power of the game, as I know the topic of that conference, but the power of career development or career game in tennis.

So I guess I'll start with, what do you mean with the term career excellence? Actually, career excellence is a new term that introduced us for psychology in order to emphasize athletic career as a part of and contribution to the lifelong career. So career excellence is defined as our flexibility to sustain healthy, successful, long-lasting career in sport and life. In that definition, healthy from developmental perspective means high resourcefulness and adaptability in order to be ready to meet current challenges and forthcoming challenges in their career. Successful means achieving individual goals in sport and other spheres of life while maintaining health and well-being. And long-lasting means longevity in sport and life. In this definition, what I like in this definition is that it emphasizes that successful athletic career is more than simply athletic success. It implies the whole person and his or her development in various spheres of life. On average, athletic career last for 10, 15 years with a several transition within. But for the career excellence pursuit, athletic retirement transition plays a key role. And it's not by chance that the career researchers studied this transition for more than five decades. I see, yeah, you took the words right out of my mouth. So it's really global. It doesn't really pertain to just how successful you are as an athlete. So it's a really wonderful message there.

But what does your research say about tennis players, in particular, their career development and major transitions in their career? Actually, preparing for this interview, I searched for the literature about tennis players' careers. There is some, but not much. And I found two types of research. First is, I would say, managerial type of studies that addressing how players proceed within the tennis ranking system and when they need to achieve the certain rank in order to progress to the top players in the world. Here is the focus, one so-called vertical career, which is about how athletes change their national or international status or climb up or down within the ranking ladder. As these studies show, dynamics of ranking is non-linear. That means with ups and downs. But what development is behind these dynamics? How and why some athletes become more successful than others? To answer this question, we need to address the social science, for example, sport psychology research, one so-called horizontal career. Horizontal career is about how athletes develop mastery, resourcefulness, adaptability, related professional and personal reputation. And I would like to talk a little bit about what appeared from these type of studies. Just very brief overview. Absolutely. First of all, tennis is early specialization sports with all pluses and minuses of early specialization sports. Pluses are quite obvious.
